the collagen content of the endomyocardial region of transplanted human myocardium is not only a reliable indicator of the collagen content of transplanted hearts, but also of the entire human myocardium.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
collagen content in the normal and in the transplanted human myocardium is not uniform.
in heart transplant recipients the collagen content of the endomyocardial subendocardial biopsy is representative for the collagen content in all regions of the myocardium.
collagen content of right ventricular biopsy samples correlates highly with collagen content of the whole myocardium.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the collagen content of the interstitium of the left ventricle is a better predictor of left ventricular function than that of the right ventricle.
the right ventricular biopsy can be used as a surrogate for the left ventricle in terms of collagen content and distribution.
right ventricular endo-myocardial biopsy is a reliable tool to assess collagen accumulation in the left ventricular myocardium in heart transplant patients.
